newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-Alcatel cuts loss, sees 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Alcatel cuts loss, sees 1996 profit.

text.p: France's largest industrial group Alcatel Alsthom said on Thursday it had cut its first half loss and it predicted a profit for 1996, after in 1995 posting the biggest loss in French corporate history.

Chairman Serge Tchuruk said that the company was on line to break even for 1996, before asset gains, and he added the sale of a 25 percent stake in mobile telecommunications company Cofira to British Telecommunications Plc would allow it to post a 1996 profit of "several billion francs".

Cofira is a holding company controlled by Generale des Eaux. BT is buying the stake as part of a deal in which it takes a 25 percent participation in Generale's Cegetel, for 1.1 billion pounds ($1.7 billion) and the share capital of BT France.

Cofira, which owns with Vodafone and SBC Corp France's second-biggest mobile telecoms group SFR, will be included in Cegetel -- a new Generale unit aiming to become France's second biggest telecommunications operator after France Telecom following liberalisation of the sector after 1998.
Germany's Mannesmann is also a Cegetel partner.

Alcatel said it had posted a first half loss of 400 million francs ($77.7 million), against 1.2 billion francs in the first six months of 1995. The 1996 loss was at the low end of analysts' expectations. Its operating income, however, fell to 0.5 billion francs from 1.4 billion. Sales were slightly down to 74.3 billion francs from 78.3 billion.
Alcatel lost 26.6 billion in 1995 after heavy charges.

"The board of directors noted that the results were in line with the action program and reflected the recent trends and the still limited effects of the current recovery plan," Alcatel said in a statement.

"The board also noticed that the effects of the plan, already more noticeable for the second half, enabled the group to aim at a return to break-even for the whole year and to foresee a significant reduction in debt, taking into account the divestments already completed as of today," the company said.
It said the group maintained its objective to achieve savings of seven billion francs per year by 1998.
Tchuruk told a news conference, "We maintain our objective for re-establishing Alcatel's profitability at a good level."

Alcatel's telecoms segment widened its operating loss to 1.1 billion francs from 0.5 billion but the group said the first half of 1996 was better than the second half of 1995 and it expected the division to post a profit in the 1996 second half.
Tchuruk said the unit's world market share in digital mobile telecoms was on course for 13 percent in 1997 and 15 percent in 1998 and it aim of 20 percent was "not beyond our reach".
Following upon a technology deal with Japan's Sharp Corp, Alcatel announced a mobile telecoms technology deal with Motorola of the U.S.
Tchuruk said that as part of the restructuring, Alcatel had announced 20,000 job losses since 1995. The group had 191,000 employees world-wide at the end of 1995.

The company recently was given permisson to acquire nuclear engineering company Framatome from the French state through the GEC-Alsthom NV joint-venture with GEC Plc. It had a minority stake in Framatome.

It is also bidding for state-owned consumer and defence electronics group Thomson SA and Tchuruk said Alcatel aimed to keep a minority stake in Thomson Multimedia, selling a stake to an Asian partner.

He said the target structure of the group was to have a core telecommunications business with 135 billion francs in sales, of which 40 billion in cables and components, 70 billion in pure telecoms and 25 billion in the systems segment. Defence, through Thomson-CSF, would also be part of the core with sales of 36 billion francs, jointly with a British and/or German partner -- GEC Plc and Daimler-Benz are expected by analysts to team up with Alcatel.
The multimedia busines, with an Asian partner, will contribute 36 billion to sales and the GEC Alsthom/Framatome company will have 80 billion in sales.
Alcatel's debt stood at 23 billion francs at the half year, against 20 billion last year, for gearing of 62 percent.

Alcatel is half way through its planned 10 billion franc disposal programme and Tchuruk said with the Cofira stake sale total disposals in 1996 could be 11 billion francs -- cutting debt and gearing significantly.
Alcatel shares closed 2.49 percent, or 10 francs, higher at 411 francs.
